faqHeading.intro: Answers on surface levels, manhole maintenance, reference-target projects and the information needed for a suitable configuration.

faqs.question: What does a wireless radar distance sensor measure?
paragraphs: A radar distance sensor uses reflected radio signals to measure the distance from its measurement reference to a target surface. The Hitelecom H Series sends readings for remote monitoring. With an agreed reference and installation, distance data can support water level, tank level, bulk-material level or changes in target position.

faqs.question: How do I choose the range and measurement performance?
paragraphs: Use the nearest and farthest target positions to define the required range. The published H310-MW012 reference specifies 0.3–12 m, ±1 mm accuracy under 25°C Hitelecom laboratory conditions, and a 1 mm reading resolution. Share the target material and installation geometry so Hitelecom can review the appropriate configuration, including requests for other ranges.

faqs.question: How is a distance reading converted into level or inventory?
paragraphs: For a fixed sensor mounted vertically above the surface, level is calculated from the configured reference height minus the measured distance to the surface. Volume uses the vessel geometry or a calibrated tank table. For bulk solids, the mounting position and surface profile also matter; a local level reading supports inventory planning when interpreted with the agreed vessel and material information.

faqs.question: Can radar distance monitoring be used for liquids and bulk solids?
paragraphs: Radar is used for liquid surfaces and for bulk materials such as grain, pellets and aggregates. Selection depends on the material, surface conditions, vessel shape and accessible mounting position. Share the medium, filling method and expected environment with Hitelecom to review a suitable configuration for your tank, silo, hopper or open-water site.

faqs.question: How can manhole level data support sediment and blockage checks?
paragraphs: A fixed radar above a sewer or drain chamber observes the exposed water surface. Water-level trends, compared with rainfall, pumping and downstream conditions, can help the maintenance team select locations for inspection. Where the chamber is dry or emptied and the deposit surface is exposed, its local height can be assessed against a known chamber datum after confirming the target return.

Specify whether you need water level, exposed deposit height or a submerged sludge interface. The submerged interface is a separate measurement task requiring an appropriate instrument; water-surface distance alone does not identify the amount or location of a pipe blockage.

faqs.question: How are distance changes used in structural movement projects?
paragraphs: A defined target can be observed from an independent, stable reference. The difference between the current gap and its baseline is a relative change along the measuring axis. For a settlement interpretation, establish a vertical measuring arrangement or validated survey geometry, with periodic checks of the reference.

Specify the required observable change and monitoring interval, then review target size, alignment, environmental effects and on-site repeatability with the project engineer. These are proposed selection briefs: the published H310-MW012 laboratory distance accuracy is a model reference, rather than a validated field settlement performance specification.
For a joint or bearing gap, the mounting member and opposing target define a relative opening. Independent survey information is needed when the project also requires absolute movement.

faqs.question: What is the difference between radar and ultrasonic level measurement?
paragraphs: Radar uses electromagnetic waves; ultrasonic measurement uses sound waves. Air temperature changes the speed of sound used in ultrasonic measurement; radar does not depend on sound speed. Their response to changing air conditions, dust, vapour and surface conditions differs. Both need an appropriate measuring path and installation. Choose by the medium, required range, available mounting space and site conditions; for foam, condensation or deposits, include those details in the application review.

faqs.question: Where should a non-contact radar distance sensor be installed?
paragraphs: Use a rigid mounting point with a clear measuring path to the intended surface or target. For level monitoring, plan the mounting position around the vessel shape, fill stream and internal structures, and keep the full operating range within the selected configuration. Establish the measurement reference and verify readings at representative levels during commissioning.

faqs.question: How are wireless connectivity and reporting configured?
paragraphs: The H Series offers 4G, NB-IoT and LoRa options by configuration. Match the network to site coverage and the destination platform, then define sampling, scheduled reporting and alert requirements. The H310-MW012 datasheet lists more than 10 years at two-hour reporting; actual service life depends on the supplied power configuration, sensing activity, network conditions and temperature.

faqs.question: What information should I provide for a radar distance sensor quotation?
paragraphs: Send the application, target material, minimum and maximum measuring distances, mounting position and approximate quantity. A site photo or vessel drawing helps define the measuring path. Include ambient and process conditions, the required reading and reporting intervals, wireless coverage, platform requirements and the level or distance events you want to monitor.

sources.use: Technical examples of distance and alignment monitoring; exclude safety/control claims from a battery periodic-reporting Hitelecom page.

sources.title: Hitelecom Radar Distance Sensor
sources.use: Current family page claims a wider customizable range and a one-hour battery profile. These differ from the specific model PDF; do not blend them into a universal H310-MW012 specification.

sources.title: Hitelecom H310-MW012 Datasheet
sources.use: Model reference: 300–12,000 mm range, ±1 mm accuracy at 25°C in Hitelecom Lab, 1 mm reading resolution, less than 20° beam, IP68, −30 to +75°C operation, 4G/NB-IoT/LoRa options. The table battery profile is two-hour reporting; it is not a field displacement acceptance test or proof of hazardous-area approval.

sources.title: Level measurement in the sewer network
sources.use: Primary industry example of overhead radar measuring wastewater/rainwater level in sewer networks. Humidity, condensation and foam are identified process challenges.

sources.title: Gully — level measurement
sources.use: Primary industry example of gully-level trends supporting deposit and blockage maintenance planning. This is evidence for the application class; it is not proof that H310-MW012 measures sediment beneath standing water.

sources.title: Turbimax CUS71D ultrasonic interface sensor
sources.use: Sedimentation-interface measurement is addressed by a submerged ultrasonic interface sensor. A free-space radar aimed at a water surface is a different measurement task.

sources.title: Silos for bulk solids — level measurement
sources.use: Primary bulk-solids radar application example covering silos, stockpiles and bunkers. Dust, abrasion, changing media, bulk density and explosion protection are selection factors. Competitor process ratings are not transferable to Hitelecom.

sources.title: RangeVue 15 radar water-level sensor
sources.use: Primary instrument description confirms the general method: distance to the water surface converted to water level/stage relative to a reference. Its 80 GHz, 8° beam and approvals belong to that product, not H310.

sources.title: Streamgaging Basics
sources.use: Water level and streamflow are different quantities. Discharge conversion requires a site-specific stage–discharge relationship based on field measurements.

sources.title: Smart Data Fusion Technology
sources.use: Structural radar line-of-sight displacement and three-dimensional movement are different outputs; combining surveying and radar can support 3D interpretation. This specialized mapping platform does not establish equivalent H310 capabilities.

sources.title: MyMo Structural Health Monitoring System
sources.use: An interferometric structural-health instrument is designed for static/dynamic behavior and multiple measurement points. A periodic single-point battery distance sensor must not inherit these capabilities by calling both products radar.

sources.title: USACE EM 1110-2-1009 Structural Deformation Surveying
sources.use: The official manual catalogue states that structural-deformation surveying has accuracy, procedure and quality-control requirements. The PDF itself could not be fetched in this tool session, so detailed clauses are not cited here.

sources.title: ATEX and explosive atmospheres
sources.use: Combustible dusts, gases and vapours can require hazardous-area classification and appropriate equipment selection. This general requirement does not prove that Hitelecom has ATEX/IECEx, mining or other Ex approval.

sources.title: Smarter Sludge Monitoring with IIoT Radars
sources.use: A competitor case describes radar above a sludge retention basin measuring the exposed process surface; it is not a claim of seeing a submerged sludge/water interface, and is not a Hitelecom customer case.

sources.title: Level and pressure instrumentation for wastewater treatment
sources.use: Primary wastewater application examples include water level upstream/downstream of screens, pump shafts and overflow basins. Paired readings can support site-specific head-loss assessment.
